4. Stop Room — Stop there and look around the room.
5. Return Seen — Meaning may return; you have seen it separate once. Word Melt — next action.

title: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
goal: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.
steps: 1. Read Bandwidth — Choose your current safe bandwidth: ONE SENTENCE, THREE SENTENCES, or FULL CONVERSATION. Set Conversation — loosen hands.
2. Choose Size — Name the purpose that must fit inside that size: acknowledge, request, pause, clarify, or repair.
3. Send Signal — Draft or say only the selected amount. Stop when the sentence limit is reached, even if more remains. Set Conversation — estimate odds.
4. Set Reopen — Name when or under what condition the next level can reopen. If you cannot offer one, state that honestly without making a false promise. Set Conversation — next action.

title: THEN / NOW SUBTITLES
goal: Flashbacks need temporal translation.
steps: 1. Alternate Lines — When memory body alarm begins, alternate lines: THEN—state one past fact; NOW—state one current difference. Now Subtitles — hear sound.
2. Include Age — Include age, place, available help, bodily freedom, and exits.
3. Keep Eyes — Keep eyes open and touch the environment after every pair. Now Subtitles — notice detail.
4. Date Location — The screen may replay; the subtitles restore date and location. Now Subtitles — next action.

title: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
goal: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
steps: 1. Name Pair — Name two emotions in the mixture and rate each with a simple low, medium, or high—not a number. Change Thing — widen gaze.
2. Hold Scene — Hold the scene steady. Choose only one variable to test: person, time, place, audience, or outcome.
3. Swap Variable — Imagine that one variable changed for ten seconds. Keep every other fact the same. Change Thing — name feeling.
4. Tag Driver — Notice which emotion moved and which stayed. Tag the changed variable as a likely driver, not a final explanation. Change Thing — next action.

title: TELL IT AT THE SPEED OF SAFETY
goal: Disclosure should increase clarity, not steal control.
steps: 1. Choose Trustworthy — Choose a trustworthy listener and agree on time, confidentiality, and a stop signal. Tell At — widen gaze.

3. Pause Orient — Pause to orient between sections. Tell At — allow opposite.
4. End Support — End with what support you want now—not what the listener guesses. Tell At — next action.

title: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
goal: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
steps: 1. Pin Forecast — Restate the fear as one visible or audible forecast—not a vague catastrophe. Make Fear — move slowly.
2. Set Clock — Give the forecast a real time window.
3. Score Odds — Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything. Make Fear — find evidence.
4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction. Make Fear — next action.

title: GROUNDING ANCHOR RELAY
goal: Rotate before one cue becomes background noise.
steps: 1. Select Different — Select four anchors from different systems: visual line, distant sound, contact pressure, joint position. Grounding Anchor — hear sound.
2. Switch Getting — Spend a short interval with each and switch before getting used to it empties it. Grounding Anchor — notice detail.
3. Finish Channel — Finish on the channel that restored the clearest present contact. Grounding Anchor — next action.

title: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
goal: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
steps: 1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high. Disassemble Alarm — widen gaze.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness. Disassemble Alarm — name sensation.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are. Disassemble Alarm — next action.

display.ritualText:
DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL

1–2 minutes · Guided reset

GOAL
The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.

1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high. Disassemble Alarm — widen gaze.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness. Disassemble Alarm — name sensation.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are. Disassemble Alarm — next action.

WIN
✓ The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.

FORMULA FLOW
Read Channels → Pick Smallest → Move Dial → Check Panel

PAUSE
New, severe, or unusual physical symptoms require medical assessment. Stop for pain, faintness, breathing difficulty, confusion, or loss of orientation.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

3. Simple — Notice the simple ongoing sense of being present through those changes. Exist Minute — allow opposite.
4. End Reclaim — Reclaim your biography on purpose at the end. Exist Minute — next action.

4. Act From Choice — Take one action from the third box. Return Their — next action.

title: TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE
goal: A boundary can close one door without burning down the whole house.
steps: 1. Name Contact — Name the contact pattern you want to change without judging the person. Down Door — press feet.
2. Pick Door — Choose exactly one access door: TIME, TOPIC, CHANNEL, LOCATION, or FREQUENCY.
3. Lower One — Lower that door by one clear level: shorter call, one topic excluded, text only, public place, or fewer contacts. Down Door — split duty.
4. Hold Setting — State the new setting and leave every other door unchanged for this round. Down Door — next action.

title: THE ROOM HAS JOBS, NOT DEMANDS
goal: A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.
steps: 1. Scan Objects — Choose four safe visible objects without moving toward them. Avoid screens if they add strain. Room Has — breathe naturally.
2. Name Jobs — For each object, name only its ordinary job: chair supports, lamp lights, cup holds, door opens.
3. Drop Demands — Say ‘not needed now’ to every function that does not serve the current safe moment. Do not remove or organise anything. Room Has — pick action.
4. Choose Helper — Choose the one object whose real function supports the next action, then use only that function. Room Has — next action.

Goal: A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.
Game Move: PLAY: Scan Objects → Drop Demands → Choose Helper
Goal + Steps:
GOAL
A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.

1. Scan Objects — Choose four safe visible objects without moving toward them. Avoid screens if they add strain. Room Has — breathe naturally.
2. Name Jobs — For each object, name only its ordinary job: chair supports, lamp lights, cup holds, door opens.
3. Drop Demands — Say ‘not needed now’ to every function that does not serve the current safe moment. Do not remove or organise anything. Room Has — pick action.
4. Choose Helper — Choose the one object whose real function supports the next action, then use only that function. Room Has — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Choose Helper.
Win / Reward: ✓ A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.
Formula Flow: Scan Objects → Name Jobs → Drop Demands → Choose Helper
Safety:
PAUSE
Stop for visual pain, dizziness, nausea, disorientation, compulsive scanning, or any real emergency requiring immediate action.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

3. Undeliverable — If no address is useful, Notice it undeliverable. Give Thought — next action.

title: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
goal: Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.
steps: 1. Run Pulse — Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it. Find Working — move slowly.
2. Full Stop — Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Read Strain — Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting. Find Working — pick action.
4. Set Gear — Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio. Find Working — next action.

title: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
goal: Several clues can be one echo wearing different clothes.
steps: 1. Name Clues — Name up to five clues currently supporting the worried conclusion. Five Clues — soften shoulders.
2. Link Sources — Imagine a line between clues that came from the same person, event, article, assumption, mood, or repeated retelling.
3. Collapse Copies — Collapse every linked cluster into one source family; do not count its echoes separately. Five Clues — notice detail.
4. Recheck Claim — Recheck the claim using the number and quality of independent families that remain. Five Clues — next action.

2. Name Boundary — Then name one boundary, skill, loyalty, or value you can carry forward without claiming the event was beneficial. Carry Forward — split duty.
3. Let Value — Let the value belong to you, not to the harm. Carry Forward — next action.

3. Return To Life — Then do one normal task that shows how you want to live now. Give Big — next action.

title: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
goal: Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.
steps: 1. Choose Skill — Choose one familiar, low-risk task with clear external feedback. Put Commentator — breathe naturally.
2. Centre Feedback — Put sight, touch, sound, or the work result in the centre of attention.
3. Demote Voice — When self-commentary appears, let it continue faintly at the edge without answering or silencing it. Put Commentator — estimate odds.
4. Finish Unit — Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections. Put Commentator — next action.

goal: Every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent.

2. Spot Amplifier — Keep what each amplifies and hides. Rotate Observation — notice detail.
3. Choose Position — Choose the position best suited to the upcoming task rather than declaring any one neutral. Rotate Observation — next action.

title: THE MILLISECOND BEFORE THE NAME
goal: What you notice exists briefly before concept files it.
steps: 1. Look Touch — Look at or touch something ordinary. Millisecond Before — loosen hands.
2. Catch Bare — Catch the first bare instant before ‘cup,’ ‘cold,’ ownership, or preference appears.
3. Don't Freeze — Do not freeze it; simply recognise the order: contact, then concept. Millisecond Before — notice detail.
4. Repeat Sound — Repeat with a sound. Millisecond Before — next action.

3. Ask Regret — Ask which regret is reversible and which conflicts most with your values. Which Regret — next action.

2. Cross Out — Strike through those identity messages mentally.

4. Notice Shift — Notice whether the preferred option changes. Remove Choice — next action.

title: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
goal: A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.
steps: 1. State Rule — Picture the rule without naming who taught it. Move Rule — widen gaze.
2. Change Context — Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
3. Compare Effects — Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting. Move Rule — challenge answer.
4. Keep Core — Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; Notice the rest as conditional. Move Rule — next action.

title: DO ONE GOOD THING WITH NO APPLAUSE BUTTON
goal: Values can survive the absence of approval.
steps: 1. Choose Safe — Perform a low-risk act you endorse and perform it without announcing, checking reactions, or fishing for reassurance. Do Good — breathe naturally.
2. Let Discomfort — Let the discomfort of no feedback rise and change. Do Good — allow opposite.
3. Review — Review the action by your values once it is done. Do Good — next action.
